messages:
jordan: Quick follow-up on the operator delegation TTL and routing weirdness we saw in canary. Noticed a spike of 503s when operator tokens rotated mid-flight. Anyone else?

maria: yep. reproducer steps: start a bulk job -> operator token rotates -> requests to user-facing svc return 503s for ~10s. logs show authz fail: "token expired" then retry fails because routing pinned to drained node.

alex: pinned routing is interesting — we have sticky session for affinity to maximize cache hits. When node goes into draining, routing still sends inflight batched streams until conn closes. If token rotates mid-stream operator can't reauth.

lena: idea: allow short-lived operator tokens to be used until active conn ends, extend grace window for previously issued tokens by 30s for in-flight streams. adds complexity to revocation.

sam: alternative: make routing fallback immediate on token verification failure -> re-route to a healthy node and re-auth using new operator token. But we need idempotency guarantees for batched requests.

maria: re-route + replay might double-execute. Bulk jobs are not idempotent. We could mark op tokens with request-id trace header and have a replay filter at upstream to de-duplicate in a 1s window.

alex: de-dupe window ok for quick retries but not for long-running ops. Also extra latency. What about delegating short TTL tokens with a renewal endpoint that can handshake and return a per-conn proof without replay?

jordan: renewal handshake: operator side issues ephemeral proof bound to conn-id and seq, valid until conn close or TTL. That avoids replays but needs conn-id at auth layer and proof storage for a few seconds.

lena: storage for proofs -> central cache? we could store in node memory and replicate to fallback nodes? replication increases complexity and latency.

sam: maybe simpler: on node drain, stream a pre-emptive token-exchange to the caller service to swap tokens before actual rotation. Kinda graceful handoff.

maria: preemptive swap requires coordination window. For sudden failures (host crash) we still need fallback. combination: preemptive for drains + re-route for crashes with de-dupe heuristics.

alex: ops-bot: can you file an infra ticket to prototype preemptive swap + 30s grace for in-flight tokens? Include perf tests for batch replay and de-dupe window.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-2482 prototype operator-token-preemptive-swap + in-flight-grace 30s. Assigned to infra/eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:

jordan: ok next steps: infra implements prototype; eng-runtime tests with canary traffic; eng-security to design threat model for grace window and revocation. I'll sync in next week's authn sync.

lena: note — include metrics: count of replays, dup-detected, preemptive-swap success rate, and extra latency p50/p95.

maria: also capture failures where request non-idempotent and replay would have side effects. We'll need a safe-fallback policy flag.

sam: thanks all. documenting learnings in runbook draft after prototype.

jordan: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
